# Pilot amendment 2: explicit host identity

The first Codex treatment reached Decapod and attempted custody without declaring
a host identity. Its task used the default `unknown`; workspace authoring then
returned `AUTHORING_ACTOR_REQUIRED`. The host's automatic approval reviewer
rejected releasing that claim because it changes ownership. No source change
occurred. Preserve this failure and its claim; do not relabel it as a passing run.

Subsequent identified treatment trials use a fresh clone and an explicit stable
`DECAPOD_AGENT_ID` supplied in the launching host environment, before any kernel
operation. This is a cooperative identity label, not verified human authority.
It grants no trust, roles, approval, proof or external-write permission. No claim
from the failed trial is released, transferred, deleted or reused.

The natural objective stays unchanged and contains no Decapod command sequence.
Report the launch-identity addition as part of the treatment and adapter contract.
The initial unknown-identity result remains an independently observable activation
failure rather than being removed from the study. CLI argument errors remain
separate pre-inference failures. All outcomes, costs and unobserved boundaries
remain visible in the final comparison.
